Theme

Tools, fasteners & household repair

adze noun

classical

Plin. NH 7.198: fabricam māteriāriam Daedalus et in eā serram, asciam, perpendiculum, terebram
Plin. NH 16.207: mollissima tilia … quod citissimē asciās retundat
Vitr. 7.2.2: sūmātur ascia et, quemadmodum māteria dolātur, sīc calx in lacū mācerāta asciētur
Libellus VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae, gloss: secūris fabrī quā trabēs dolantur

ascia, asciae f.

noun, first declension

adze, the carpenter’s axe for dressing timber

Lewis & Short: “an axe for hewing wood, a carpenter’s axe”; secūris is the ordinary axe. Pliny, NH 7.198 makes Daedalus the inventor of carpentry and of its first tools; the square and the level go to Theodorus of Samos. In NH 16.207 lime wood blunts adzes fastest. In Vitruvius 7.2.2 the adze also tests slaked lime: if the lime clings to the iron like glue, it is ready for plastering.

Examples

  • Asciam mihi dā.

    Give me the adze.composed

  • «Asciam nōvī!» inquit Theodōrus. «Asciam volō!»

    I know the adze! I want the adze!Libellus VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae

  • malleus, serra, ascia, quam Bulgarī teslam vocant, secūris, terebra, scalprum, rēgula, norma, forceps, runcīna, trulla, quā tēctōrēs tēctōrium indūcunt, līnea cum perpendiculō, capsa clāvōrum

    hammer, saw, the adze the Bulgarians call tesla, axe, drill, chisel, ruler, square, pincers, plane, the trowel plasterers spread plaster with, a plumb line, a box of nailsLibellus VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae

See also hew, axe, square, plane, trowel, plumb bob, hammer, saw, nail, chisel.
